transcript:
Header: 2027-09-07 | 15:00 PT | 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jena Wei (Redwood SE), Lisa Carter (RiverMark Head of AI), Miguel Alvarez (Backend), Priya Singh (SRE)
Artifacts shared: benchmark-spreadsheet://drive/rivermark-redwood-ttft (Samir), perf-run-logs (Jena)

00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for hopping on. see you all, um, quick agenda — sync on last week's numbers, TTFT improvements from streaming, kernel sweep recap, and plan next tests.
00:28 Lisa: yep thanks Samir been looking forward to the numbers. last week we saw p50 of ~210ms on small prompts but TTFT was, like, high for a few.
00:52 Jena: right — so quick recap, we ran the default hosted endpoint and then our dedicated pilot with three kernel configs. note, the autoscaler momentarily bumped nodes during the long seq runs so ignore that one outlier in the sheet.
01:15 Miguel: question — are the TTFT numbers measuring first byte or first token? we need first token for UX gating.
01:26 Samir: good call — in the sheet TTFT is time-to-first-token (we instrumented token emit). I labelled it TTF T in one column cause the exporter mashed it up, sorry.
01:40 Priya: also curious about network overhead, we have a 20ms egress through our VPC to the Dedicated pool when we tested; that adds up.
01:55 Jena: yeah we added a network delta column, it's small but consistent. for streaming we saw a ~30-60ms reduction in TTFT for chat-style prompts because we start emitting earlier with chunked logits.
02:18 Lisa: can you explain the streaming tradeoffs again? I remember it improves TTFT but sometimes increases total tail latency?
02:28 Jena: exactly. streaming gets you earlier perceived response — you start seeing tokens sooner — but if you chop tokens into lots of small chunks it can increase per-token overhead at high throughput. there's a balance. we saw p95 increase by 80ms in one config due to small chunk sizes.
02:53 Miguel: were you batching for those streaming tests?
03:00 Jena: minimal batching — streaming tests used smaller batch windows to favor latency. for throughput tests we used continuous batching with the runtime's adaptive window.
03:18 Samir: and kernels — short version: cutlass was best for 128-seq on A100-like hardware in our testbed, Triton was close but a hair slower on TTFT; direct-metal fell behind on throughput but gave more consistent tail.
03:45 Lisa: cutlass? is that the NV cutlass library? sometimes I see it spelled cutlass but ASR turned it into cut last in the notes haha.
03:54 Jena: yep NV Cutlass math libraries; also we tested the Triton compiled kernels and a more conservative direct-metal path that skips some fused ops for stability.
04:12 Priya: how did quantization affect TTFT? we run int8 on some models in prod.
04:20 Jena: int8 reduced token compute by ~15-25% in throughput but TTFT improvements were smaller because the overhead is often memory/memory copies early in generation. still, quant helped tail latency consistency in some configs.
04:42 Miguel: sequence length — we usually expect shorter seq to be faster but workload has some 400+ token prompts. what did you see at 512?
04:52 Jena: at 512 steps, batching improves throughput but TTFT for cold calls increases due to longer KV cache warm-up if you can't reuse prefixes. we observed 30-40ms extra TTFT on average vs 128 for cold runs. hot runs with prefix cache warm reduced that delta heavily.
05:15 Lisa: sounds like prefix caching will be important if we want low TTFT for repeated system prompts.
05:25 Samir: yes, our runtime supports prefix/KV caching; Jena's notes show scenarios where enabling prefix cache cut TTFT by 60-120ms across repeated prompts.
05:40 Miguel: any weird ASR in the notes? I saw 'KV cash' once — that's 'KV cache' :)
05:47 Samir: classic.
05:50 Jena: on the kernel sweep specifics: we tested seq lens 128/256/512, cutlass vs triton vs direct-metal, and three quant modes (fp16, int8, int8 with per-channel). results in the sheet: cutlass+fp16 wins on p50 for 128, triton+fp16 slightly better at mid seq for throughput, direct-metal gives the best p95 consistency for high seq lengths.
06:25 Priya: do we have logs showing where the time is spent? tokenization, kernel dispatch, memcpy, network, etc?
06:32 Jena: yes — per-step breakdown: tokenize ~5-15ms for our prompts, memcpy and kernel launch dominate for small sequences ~40-60ms, network adds 15-25ms depending on VPC route. I've linked a perf trace in the sheet.
07:00 Lisa: great. on the Dedicated environment, are we pinned to specific GPU generations? our infra team prefers A100 but wants to understand tradeoffs.
07:12 Samir: for the pilot we're on A100s but we can run a small test on H100-like instances too. H100 improved some long-seq throughputs in our internal runs but kernel compatibility needs extra tuning.
07:30 Miguel: H100 would be ideal if we get consistent gains. what's the rough delta we've seen?
07:36 Jena: in our lab, H100 cut p50 by ~20-30% on large seq workloads but for TTFT improvements were smaller — more on steady throughput.
07:50 Lisa: any security notes we should flag for our compliance team?
07:56 Samir: we already shared SOC2 docs and the Dedicated VPC flow; we will also include KMS integration notes and audit log retention options in the next package.
08:12 Priya: please also include specific egress and IP allowlist guidance so our network team can prep.
08:20 Samir: noted — adding to action items.
08:25 Miguel: about streaming chunk sizes — you mentioned 32 token chunks earlier; what happens if we do 8 token chunks?
08:33 Jena: 8 token chunks reduce TTFT marginally but increase per-token overhead and can blow up CPU context switches at scale, so p95 goes up. we recommend 16-32 token windows as a start.
08:50 Lisa: do we have a suggested config for our chat flow? we typically use a 2-turn system+user prefix then user prompt ~40 tokens.
08:58 Jena: for that pattern, enable prefix cache, use cutlass+fp16 at seq128, streaming with 16 token chunks, minimal batching. should hit TTFT under 180ms excluding VPC egress.
09:15 Samir: (to Miguel) can you try that config on your staging workload this week? we can compare p50/p95 to the sheet.
09:23 Miguel: yes I'll run it and share logs.
09:28 Lisa: one more thing — we saw a weird stutter at 1.2s on longer prompts; is that kernel swap or GC?
09:35 Jena: likely kernel fallback for very long attention windows; the runtime may pick a different kernel path mid-run when we cross certain sequence thresholds. we can instrument to avoid runtime flipping kernels mid-request.
09:52 Priya: that sounds important for UX. can the runtime be pinned to a kernel per-model?
09:58 Jena: yes, we can pin kernel selection in the config to force a single code path; that will help predictability though may sacrifice some peak throughput.
10:12 Lisa: ok let's do that for the UX-sensitive flows.
10:18 Samir: noted. I'll include an example config.
10:22 Miguel: on costs — any ballpark on cost delta when switching from hosted to Dedicated for our expected qps?
10:30 Samir: we ran a cost projection in the sheet; Dedicated is more predictable for sustained loads and can be cheaper at scale, but there is minimum reserved capacity. I'll highlight the per-token effective costs in the updated sheet.
10:48 Lisa: thanks.
10:50 Jena: quick clarification — when we say TTF T improvements of 60ms, that's measured from request arrival at the runtime to emission of the first token. network and client-side decoding not included unless we explicitly instrument client.
11:10 Miguel: understood. we'll make sure to match instrumentation.
11:18 Samir: ok wrapping up — recap and next steps: Samir to send updated sheet with highlighted TTFTs and links; Jena will run kernel + quant sweep and share results; RiverMark to provide prompts and run staged test of suggested config; schedule infra deep-dive re: kernel pinning and network egress.
11:40 Lisa: that works for us. thanks team.
11:44 Priya: thanks all.
11:46 Samir: thanks everyone. I'll ping follow-up calendar and attach artifacts. bye.

Post-call notes: artifacts referenced — drive://rivermark-ttft-benchmarks (Samir), perf-logs://redwood/jena/kernel-sweep, config-examples://redwood/examples/pin-kernel.json

Transcription notes: minor ASR errors (KV cash -> KV cache, TT F T -> TTFT, cut last -> Cutlass).
